title: Tenant-level egress governor with jurisdictional circuit-breakers (EU-first)
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem: Several enterprise customers require strict EU-only processing and egress, with tenant-scoped allowlists/denylists and predictable fallback behavior when EU resources are unavailable. Current runtime provides coarse region hints and tenant flags but lacks a unified enforcement layer that can: (1) enforce per-tenant jurisdictional policies consistently across hosted/dedicated/private modes, (2) perform graceful fallback to compliant model variants or deny/queue requests when necessary, and (3) surface clear audit trail and metrics for compliance reviews.

This ticket implements a Tenant-level Egress Governor (TEG) and Jurisdictional Circuit-Breaker subsystem. TEG responsibilities: policy evaluation (allow/deny/route/soft-fallback), model-variant selection for fallbacks (e.g., eu-only quantized variants), backpressure/circuit-breaker decisions when EU capacity is exhausted, and audit logging with cryptographic provenance metadata. The enforcement plane (PEP) will live at the region edge and in serving proxies; a lightweight PDP will be available in-region with a global read-through cache to minimize latency.

Scope: engineering work to implement PDP/PEP integration, policy schema, tenant policy store migration, model-variant registry mapping, runtime hooks for fallback selection, audit-log format, and a canary/rollout plan with automated tests and dashboards. Does NOT include UI for Console (separate PM ticket) but will emit events the Console can consume.

Non-goals: complex consent flows, legal determinations, or multi-tenant sharding changes beyond policy metadata.

Key design principles: predictable latency (p50 increase <= 6ms on policy check), deterministic precedence (tenant explicit allowlist > tenant denylist > global), safe defaults (deny egress if policy unresolved), and auditable decisions for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant policy schema implemented and stored in the policy DB for 1000 test tenants
Policy enforcement reachable from edge proxies with mean added latency <= 6ms (measured under 99th percentile traffic conditions)
Circuit-breaker triggers correctly when EU-backed capacity falls below configured thresholds and transitions traffic to configured fallback variants or returns 451-status with compliance code
Fallback model-variant mapping supports at least three variants (eu-standard, eu-quantized-4bit, local-cpu-safe) and runtime selects variant based on policy and capacity signals
Audit log records contain tenant_id, decision_id, policy_version, input_region_hint, final_route, fallback_reason (if any), and SHA256(provenance) and are available to retention/exports for 7 years
End-to-end regression tests and synthetic canary harness run in CI and pass against a staging deployment
Monitoring dashboards show fallback_rate, deny_rate, decision_latency_p50/p95, and circuit_breaker_state with alerting thresholds configured
design_notes: Architecture: PEP in edge proxies -> local PDP (in-region) with global policy-store read-through cache. PEP uses short-lived decision cache keyed by (tenant, route, region_hint, model_family)
Policy schema: allowlist and denylist both accept CIDR ranges, org IDs, and explicit model-family tags. Precedence: tenant allowlist > tenant denylist > global allow/deny > emergency-override (ops)
Jurisdiction detection: honor X-Region-Hint when present from Console or customer network; fallback to IP geolocation. Store detection confidence score with every decision
Circuit-breaker: state machine (CLOSED, HALF_OPEN, OPEN) pegged to EU capacity metrics (available_gpus, queue_depth, avg_latency). OPEN state triggers deterministic fallback graph evaluation

Fallback graph: ranked list of variants with policy-level weights and hard-fail thresholds. Example: [eu-standard -> eu-quantized-4bit -> local-cpu-safe]. If no variant satisfies policy, return 451 with compliance metadata
Audit & provenance: decisions signed with internal signing key; logs shipped to customer-scoped retention buckets where required
Policy mutability: tenant admins and Ops can stage changes. We will support policy versioning for safe rollbacks
Performance: synchronous PDP with <5ms targets using in-memory caches; fallback to async PDP read for rare cache-miss scenarios with default-deny temporary behavior
tradeoffs: Central PDP offers easier governance but increases latency; solution uses in-region PDP + global cache to balance latency and consistency
Default-deny on ambiguous policy ensures compliance but can cause customer-visible errors; mitigating with clear error codes and console guidance
Signing/audit provides strong provenance but adds write volume to log pipelines and storage costs (tradeoff accepted for high-risk tenants)
Supporting many variant types increases operational complexity for runtime scheduling; initial scope limits to three variants per model-family
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag + internal-only canary (internal tenants) — validate policy schema and audit logs
Phase 1: 5% EU customer canary for tenants who opt-in, monitor fallback_rate and decision_latency for 72 hours
Phase 2: 20% expansion with SRE on-call and automated rollback on policy-violation alerts
Phase 3: Broad rollout for all EU-flagged tenants with announcement and console integrations
Rollback strategy: feature-flag off -> PDP returns cached 'global allow' to avoid mass denial (ops manual rollback available)
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation engine and precedence rules
Integration test: PEP <-> PDP over simulated cache-miss and high-latency PDP scenarios
E2E synthetic: create test tenants with EU-only policies and run traffic until circuit-breaker transitions, assert fallback path correctness
Chaos: simulate EU region outage and validate auto-fallback to quantized variants and final error codes
Compliance test: export of audit logs and verification of signature and hash chain
